title: Build an Active Ingredient Shortlist
summary: Turn a formula concept into a focused set of compatible grades and verification steps.
intro: Start with the formula architecture and the goal the ingredient needs to serve.
sections: Note the phase structure, pH, heat exposure and target sensory profile.
Check identity, assay, solubility, carrier and processing conditions.
Identify stability, microbiological and claim-related tests for the finished formula.
content: A practical process for comparing cosmetic active ingredients.

title: What to Review in a Botanical Extract
summary: Origin, extraction, carrier and marker content affect how an extract fits a formula.
intro: Two extracts with the same plant name can differ in carrier, color and performance.
sections: Review botanical name, plant part, origin and extraction route.
Powder and liquid extracts bring different solvents and processing needs.
Confirm markers, microbiological limits, contaminants, color and odor.
content: Evaluate botanical extracts beyond their marketing name.

title: Choose Preservation for the Finished Formula
summary: pH, water content, packaging and manufacturing conditions all affect preservation.
intro: A preservative blend cannot be approved independently from the finished cosmetic formula.
sections: Consider water content, packaging, botanicals and consumer use.
Confirm pH, temperature, solubility and incompatibilities by grade.
Run suitable microbiological and preservative-efficacy testing.
content: Select and validate preservation as part of the complete formula.
